title: Best Half Marathons in Southeast Asia
intro: The half marathon is the region's default distance, and the range reflects that: everything from major-city races with tens of thousands of entrants to small municipal runs where the 21.1km is the longest thing on offer. Coverage is heaviest in the Philippines and Malaysia, with strong showings in Indonesia and Thailand. Because most events stack 21.1km alongside 10K and 5K legs at the same venue, a half marathon here is usually one option within a larger race day rather than a standalone event.

faqs.question: Do I need to travel far to find a half marathon in Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Rarely. The distance appears on race calendars across all the major countries in the region almost every weekend of the season, and most capital cities host several a year. The harder question is usually which one to pick rather than whether one exists near your dates.

faqs.question: What start times should I expect for a Southeast Asian half marathon?
faqs.answer: Very early. Flag-offs between 4am and 6am are standard across the region because daytime heat and humidity make later starts unsafe. Factor this into accommodation: staying near the start line matters more here than it would for an equivalent race in a temperate climate.
